## Objective

The model estimates the incremental screening cost per severe thalassaemia birth averted
for four screening strategies in Thailand. Each strategy is compared with "no
screening".

## Strategies

1. Post-conception screening
2. Pre-conception screening using CBC and Hb typing with targeted DNA analysis
3. Pre-conception screening using universal DNA analysis
4. Combined pre- and post-conception screening

## Outcomes

The model reports:

- incremental cost in THB;
- the proportion of severe thalassaemia births averted; and
- the ICER in THB per severe thalassaemia birth averted.

The deterministic base-case results are written to
`outputs/tables/base_case_results.csv`.

## Base-case carrier prevalence

Individual carrier prevalence is 0.16. Under random mating, the corresponding
couple probabilities are:

\[
P(\text{both carriers}) = p^2 = 0.0256,
\]

\[
P(\text{one carrier}) = 2p(1-p) = 0.2688,
\]

and

\[
P(\text{neither carrier}) = (1-p)^2 = 0.7056.
\]

## Willingness-to-pay definition

The cost-effectiveness threshold represents the discounted lifetime cost of
managing severe thalassaemia. All supported analyses call
`calculate_wtp_thresholds()` from `R/economic_functions.R`, using:

- 2005 exchange rate: 40.22 THB per USD;
- inflation adjustment rate (from 2005 THB to 2024 THB): 166.22 / 111.2;
- annual discount rate: 3%;
- time horizon: 30 years; and
- annual 2005 management costs of USD 224.90, 562.76, and 782.70 for the low,
  base, and high thresholds.
